content.intro: This lesson focuses on json type identification and connects the PDF syllabus topics to a small, inspectable example. Work from the intended data model, write down the expected result, then verify syntax and semantics with the target tool.
content.why_it_matters: JSON Type Identification matters because structured-data files sit between people, tools, services, and deployment systems. A clear contract and repeatable checks make the result easier to maintain and safer to consume.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: JSON strings use double quotes and defined escapes; numbers follow a strict grammar; booleans are lowercase literals; and null differs from a missing member. Parsers create runtime values that can have language-specific numeric and null behavior.

content_blocks.title: What you will cover

Distinguishing values that look similar when printed.; Inspecting types after parsing. Common type-conversion mistakes.. Treat each as part of a workflow: define what the data should mean, represent it consistently, and test how the chosen implementation interprets it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: JSON Type Identification
content_blocks.expected_output: Parsed types differ even where printed forms may look similar: number, boolean, string, object, array, and null.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Save as example.json and run `python -m json.tool example.json`. This validates JSON syntax and formats the file; it does not validate a JSON Schema or application business rules.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the starting fixture before each test. Change one field, indentation level, parser option, or schema constraint at a time, then compare the result with the prediction.
content_blocks.limitations: This snippet is a reference/example, not evidence that the CodeLeaf browser executes JSON/YAML parsing, shell commands, or Python. Validate locally with a named parser or tool before relying on it.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating readable text as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Syntax and visual formatting cannot establish data types, schema conformance, or application-specific meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse, validate against the intended contract, and test a valid plus an invalid fixture.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every parser interprets the feature identically.
common_mistakes.why: Format versions, schema choices, library defaults, and product-specific restrictions affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the exact parser/version and test the target environment.

common_mistakes.why: Missing fields, wrong types, duplicate keys, or ambiguous scalars may still break consumers.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep valid, invalid, and boundary fixtures in version control.
